PROJECT 1 · ACADEMIC PROJECT

Beauty Parlour Management System (BPMS)

The problemSmall beauty parlours rely on phone calls and paper registers. Customers need a simple way to book, and the owner needs one place to manage the business.
TypeAcademic project (BCA)
My roleWireframes in Figma, then UI design and development.
ToolsFigma, PHP, MySQL, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap.

Wireframe to Final Screen

Each screen was planned in Figma first, then built.

Payment Method

After booking, the customer picks how to pay: Pay at Parlour (cash), or eSewa and Khalti in sandbox mode. The invoice number and the total payable are shown above the options so the amount is clear before choosing.

Design Decisions

  • Booking form limited to service, date, time and an optional message on one screen.
  • Get Appointment button repeated after the services section.
  • Admin dashboard with a fixed left menu for services, appointments, customers, invoices and reports.
  • Colour-coded summary cards for customers, appointments, services and sales.

What I Would Improve Next

  • Use one colour palette and shared components across the customer site, admin panel and chat.
  • Keep navigation labels on one line using Auto Layout.
  • Move the home page hero text to one side so it does not cover the image.

What I Would Test Next

  • Ask 3–5 people to book an appointment and note where they get confused.
  • Compare the wireframe flow with the built flow to check nothing was lost.
PROJECT 2 · ACADEMIC PROJECT

Bloomify: Flower E-commerce Platform

The problemShoppers need to see price, stock and order status quickly, and the owner needs to manage orders without touching the database.
TypeAcademic project (BCA)
My roleUI design and development of the storefront and the admin panel.
ToolsPHP, MySQL, HTML, CSS, responsive layouts.

Design Decisions

  • Green and gold palette to feel premium and natural.
  • Consistent product cards: image, name, price, stock badge and actions in the same place.
  • One visual language for the storefront and the admin panel.
  • Status labels with consistent colours (Active, Pending, Processing).
  • Order confirmation showing order ID, amount and status.

Key Screens

More Customer Screens

Featured Categories gives shoppers a fast route into the catalog by flower type, and Fresh Arrivals highlights new products directly on the homepage to encourage exploration.

The login screen uses a soft, illustrated graphic to make account access feel warm and welcoming rather than transactional, while keeping the form itself minimal and focused.

Admin Panel

I designed and built the full admin panel so the owner can manage the shop without touching the database. It mirrors the customer site’s visual identity but is organized around data: tables, filters and quick actions.

What I Would Test Next

  • Ask 3–5 people to find and buy a bouquet without help.
  • Check that the stock badge and discount price are noticed before the buttons.
  • Time how long the owner needs to update a pending order.

Figma Practice

After my BPMS wireframes, I practiced grids, color theory, typography, Auto Layout, components and variants, and visual effects in Figma.

Flower Website Prototype

  • Home page with Home, About, Product, Category and Contact Us links.
  • Back to Top link and a footer with contact details.

Wallpaper App Prototype

  • Mobile wallpaper screen with download and save icons.
  • Thanks for Downloading screen with a Go Back to Home button.

Glassmorphism Visiting Card

  • A frosted-glass card built with background blur, a linear gradient stroke, a subtle inner shadow and a noise texture over colored shapes, to practice depth, layering and effects.

Background Blur: Before and After

  • The same photo with a sharp half and a blurred half, made to understand how background blur differs from layer blur and when each is useful.

Responsive Landing Page

  • Navigation bar, hero, stats, features and call-to-action buttons.
  • Built with Auto Layout in a green and black palette.

Digital Agency Landing Page

  • Hero, project showcase, client testimonial and closing call to action.

The Three Pillars: Auto Layout, Components and Variants

These three Figma features turn a single screen into a design that scales, so I practiced each one separately and then used them together.

Auto Layout

I rebuilt a profile card with nested Auto Layout: a header row set to space-between, navigation tags that wrap onto a new line, and Hug, Fill and Fixed resizing. I resized the card from wide to narrow to confirm that it reflows without manual adjustments.

Components

I created a reusable button component so every button in a design stays consistent, and a change to the main component updates all of its instances. I then used instances of the button to lay out a sign-up screen.

Variants

I added Default, Hover, Focused and Disabled variants to the button inside one component set, so each state can be switched from the properties panel instead of drawing a new button for every state.
